'''''Gladiolus dalenii''''' is a [[species]] of [[flowering plant]] in the iris [[family (botany)|family]] Iridaceae. It is one of the most widely distributed species of ''Gladiolus'', ranging from eastern South Africa and Madagascar throughout tropical Africa and into western Arabia.<ref name=POWO_437402-1/> It is the main parental species of the large flowering grandiflora hybrids. This species is also unusual in its genus in including [[Polyploidy|diploid]], tetraploid and hexaploid races. The hybrids produced from it are often tetraploids.<ref name="pbs">{{cite web | last = | first = | authorlink = | vauthors = | title = Southern African Gladiolus | publisher = Pacific Bulb Society | date = | url = http://www.pacificbulbsociety.org/pbswiki/index.php/SouthernAfricanGladiolusThree | format = | doi = | accessdate = 2 June 2013 | archiveurl =  | archivedate = }}</ref>

It produces five tall flower spikes of yellow to scarlet flowers, often streaked red over a yellow ground color, generally with a yellow throat.<ref name="pbs"/> In cultivation, it prefers a light sandy neutral to slightly acid soil with a pH between 6.5 and 7 in a sunny sheltered position and requires a stony gritty loam.
